root_cause.text: Missing page deallocation on error paths in `tap_get_user_xdp()` causes a memory leak when a frame is too short or `build_skb()` fails, because the page allocated by `vhost_net_build_xdp()` is not freed before jumping to the error label.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that "Both paths jump to the err label without freeing the page that vhost_net_build_xdp() allocated for the frame." The patch adds `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data))` before both `err = -EINVAL` and `err = -ENOMEM` jumps. Additionally, the CVE description and commit note mention that `tap_sendmsg()` discards the return value, so the caller never frees the page on failure, exacerbating the leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak by releasing page reference when XDP buffer is too short in tap_get_user_xdp.
intent_record.what: Added a call to put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data)) inside the condition that checks if the XDP buffer data length is less than ETH_HLEN, before setting the error code and jumping to the err label.
intent_record.how: When an XDP buffer is too short to contain an Ethernet header, the function now releases the page reference held by the buffer, preventing a memory leak caused by an unbalanced page reference count.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added put_page call to release the page backing the XDP buffer when skb allocation fails, fixing a memory leak in tap_get_user_xdp.

intent_record.how: The change ensures that the page backing the XDP buffer is released (reference count decremented) when socket buffer allocation fails, preventing a memory leak of that page.
